full_judgment: 18. We note also from the judgment of the trial Court that emphasis has been put on the fact that plaintiff No. 1, Surendra Sikder was not produced to depose in the case. It was observed that he was a vital witness, inasmuch as the defendants' alleged that it was plaintiff No. 1 who approached them with an offer of sale of the disputed land. It was further contended   by the defendants that Surendra went to the registry office along with his mother and paternal uncle. Only he could have denied the allegations made by the defendants in their written statement. But his failure to depose in support of the plaintiffs' case was rightly held by the trial Court to lead to an adverse presumption against the plaintiffs' case. Similarly, it was suggested by the defendants that 4.62 acres of land was returned by a deed of sale in favour of the six sons of the two plaintiffs and that deed was witnessed by plaintiff No. 1. Since this was pleaded in the written statement of the defendants, it was incumbent upon the plaintiffs to produce plaintiff No. 1 to deny his signature as witness in the deed of sale by which 4.62 acres of land out of the suit land was returned to the sons of the plaintiffs.
